input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4), provided that Client timely pays all contested amounts.
input.rationale: The agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection or verification right over Client's usage, records or systems. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books", "verify" and "monitor" return nothing, and the two candidate sections confirm this: Compensation (§ 5/6) runs the wrong way for the vendor — Client is entitled to supporting documentation and to contest charges (p0047) — and the Client covenants in § 8 impose compliance and access-restriction duties without any TrueLink right to examine Client's premises, records or systems. Section 2(e) likewise gives Client, not TrueLink, access to usage statistics and raw log files (p0037). The only vendor self-help right is § 8(f), under which TrueLink may "implement technical mechanisms" to prevent spamming or illegal activity (p0058); that operates within TrueLink's own hosted Interface environment and is neither a usage/records audit nor access to Client systems, so it does not engage the walk-away trigger. With no audit obligation binding us, the rule's protective parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, no system access) cannot be exceeded, so the position is better than preferred. We should not insert an audit right the vendor has not asked for, as that would create an obligation against our own party; we simply resist any audit language added in later drafts unless it meets the once-per-12-months / 30 days' notice / independent auditor / vendor-cost standard.
